title: Ground instances: term models and Herbrand's theorem
summary: Replace universal, equality-free formulas by their closed-term instances and construct a model directly from a propositional truth assignment.
abstract: A universal statement must hold for every object, so testing only the objects named by closed terms may seem insufficient. For formulas built from relations, without equality or quantifiers inside the statement, these instances completely determine whether a model exists. A truth assignment to all the closed instances becomes a model whose objects are the terms themselves. We prove this construction carefully, then use propositional compactness to show that failure already appears in finitely many instances. Adding one fresh constant handles languages with no closed terms, while an equality example explains why the theorem needs its stated restriction.

based_on.title: Logic and Mechanized Reasoning (Release 0.1)
based_on.pages: §16.2, Completeness of resolution (ground instances and the term-model argument)
